thread:
alex: Heads-up — deploybot just bumped search-service from 1.8.2 -> 1.8.3 during the night window. Noticed it's a backport-only fix with no API changes.
release-bot: deploybot: created tag v1.8.3 and published artifact search-service:v1.8.3 at 2024-03-21T02:14Z :robot_face:
maria: Wait, was that a semantic patch we wanted? I thought internal cherrypicks should get buildmeta not a semver patch.
sophie: Historically we've used patch for any bugfix shipped to prod. But that makes the public semver jump even when nothing changed for customers.
matt: Agree with maria — for backports that only affect infra (e.g., logging tweaks) I'd prefer buildmeta. Keeps mainline semver cleaner.
alex: The deploybot config currently has:
```
auto_bump: patch
allow_buildmeta: true
buildmeta_template: "ci.%Y%m%d%H%M"
```
Is deploybot ignoring allow_buildmeta for certain repos?
chris: It did for search-service because the release job picked the "deps-only" heuristic as false. So it followed auto_bump: patch.
maria: Can we refine the heuristic? like: if only files under tools/ or infra/ or docs/ then buildmeta; if code under pkg/ or public_api/ then patch? :thinking:
sophie: That would help. Also some package managers strip buildmeta — go modules includes it but npm/yarn normally ignore buildmeta when resolving ranges. We need to be careful for client SDKs.
matt: Good point. For SDKs we should always patch; for internal services buildmeta is fine.
alex: Proposal: update deploybot rules:
- repo-type: sdk -> always patch
- repo-type: service -> patch only if public_api touched or user-facing bug
- otherwise -> buildmeta tag for backports/infra-only
Also add an override `force_patch: true` that release leads can set in the PR.
chris: Implementation note — releasebot can inspect changed paths. Example matcher:
```
service_public_paths:
  - "src/public/**"
  - "pkg/api/**"
```
If none match => use buildmeta.
maria: That sounds reasonable. One more: change windows. During change windows we prefer patch bumps for predictability, even for infra-only? My worry is customers pinning versions and expecting monotonic increases.
sophie: I'd say during scheduled change window (09:00-17:00 PST) we default to patch; off-window prefer buildmeta unless critical.
matt: Also we should standardize release notes generation. If buildmeta-only, skip public release notes but add internal changelog entry.
alex: So final decision for this thread:
- update deploybot heuristics to prefer buildmeta for infra-only backports
- repo-specific exceptions for SDKs -> always patch
- change-window override -> prefer patch
- add `force_patch` and `force_buildmeta` flags on PR template
- release notes: buildmeta-only => internal note only
chris: I'll open a small RFC + PR to change the deploybot config and add the flags to the PR template. Assigning to @chris and @maria :+1:
maria: Thanks. Can we also add a check in the release validation that warns when a buildmeta was used for an SDK repo? That'll catch edge cases.
chris: yep will add a linter rule and a CI warning step.
alex: Great. Also add rollback criteria to the RFC: if a buildmeta-backport causes regressions we still rollback same as patch (no special handling), but call it out in the runbook.
sophie: noted. I'll update the runbook with the rollback steps and the tagging examples.
matt: Example tags we should document in runbook:
- patch: v1.8.4
- buildmeta: v1.8.3+ci.20240321
- forced patch override: v1.8.3
chris: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/deploybot/pull/412 — includes heuristics + PR template changes
alex: Thanks everyone. We'll merge once the RFC gets a +1 from release and infra. Closing thread. :shipit:
